content: The Annals of Internal Medicine (Ann Intern Med) is an academic medical journal published by the American College of Physicians (ACP). It focuses on publishing research articles and reviews in the field of internal medicine. The current editor of the journal is Harold C. Sox. The journal is one of the most frequently cited general clinical medical journals, surpassed only by JAMA, The Lancet, and the New England Journal of Medicine. In 2005, its circulation was approximately 90,000. The Annals of Internal Medicine was established in 1927 and has been published twice monthly since 1988. Edward Huth, a former Editor-in-Chief, has documented the history of the journal. The journal has introduced several innovations in medical publishing, including: In 1987, it proposed the use of structured abstracts, which were first published in the April issue of that year. In 1994, it conducted research on the effects of peer review. In 1997, it included guidelines for the Bayesian interpretation of significance testing in its instructions for authors. In 1999, it introduced Summaries for Patients for original research articles. In 2004, it added a Limitations section to its standard structured abstracts. An online archive of issues dating back to 1993 is available on the journal's website in both text and PDF formats (PDFs are available from 1999 onward). Articles older than six months are freely accessible, and all papers are provided free of charge to developing countries.
